_readme: Back-test corpus: dates whose Jain panchang values are recorded independently of this engine.
WORKFLOW — this file is designed to be filled in by a human, not by the engine.
Every entry starts with "verified": false. An entry is only ENFORCED once a human has
checked it against a primary source (Shatabdi Panchang 1950-2050, source-id CP-1950-2050,
or a published Digambar panchang) and flipped the flag to true.
Unverified entries are still RUN and reported as a diff table, so mismatches are visible
immediately — but they cannot fail the build, because an unverified expectation is not
evidence. This keeps the harness honest: the engine is never declared correct against
data nobody checked, and never declared broken against a date that might itself be wrong.
"expect" fields are all optional. Omit any field you cannot vouch for; only the fields
precise sunrise matters for a boundary case.
Tithi convention: a day is named for the tithi prevailing at SUNRISE, not at noon.
ANCHOR (vyapini rule): which moment of the day decides the tithi. 'udaya' = at
sunrise (the general rule). 'pradosha' = just after sunset - Diwali/Mahavir
Nirvana are fixed this way, lamps being lit while Kartik Amavasya runs.
'nishitha' = local midnight - Sharad Purnima moon-viewing. 'madhyahna' = apparent
noon. Using the wrong anchor shifts a festival by a full day.
Real sunrise/sunset for lat/lng is computed per entry; there is no fixed clock time.
